topologyProof.argmaxMechanism: one CSS Grid element per candidate

lazyRunner.note: This is the least-DOM top-two variant, but it adds a second 256-way Grid evaluation to every selected hot visit before deciding whether exact fallback is needed.

corpusSemantics.reason: No browser-realized split-GSUB candidate deltas exist for the 1,024-state corpus; the fixture ±2 bound is empirical and cannot be promoted to a portable corpus proof.

rejectionReasons: GSUB selects group-specific glyph rows but does not perform argmax; the maximum still requires 256 overlaid Grid candidates per group.
The router needs groups 0 and 1 simultaneously, so cv01 feature selection cannot share one 256-candidate top grid between them.
Two top grids require the same 512 candidate elements as retained K=2, so zero upper candidates are removed.
A margin needs a winner-masked runner Grid: 256 additional candidates per selected hot visit, or 512 additional candidates if both runners are eager.
Each split scorer candidate shapes 13 glyphs instead of the retained exact scorer's 12.
browserGateReasons: The required 512-row removal is impossible: the lower-bound GSUB top layer still has 512 candidate elements.
Even before the runner, split-GSUB glyph work rises from 12 to 13 glyphs per candidate.
The requested offline gate therefore fails, so no HTML/browser topology or timing run is authorized.
